### From Foundation Models to Production-Grade Agentic AI Systems

> **Audience**: Staff Engineers, AI Platform Architects, and Agentic AI Practitioners
> **Depth**: Beginner → Enterprise Production
> **Last Updated**: 2026

sections.title: 1. Platform Overview & Evolution
sections.body:
### 1.1 From Vertex AI to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform

Google's Vertex AI was originally launched in 2021 as a unified ML platform that consolidated AutoML Tables, AutoML Vision, AI Platform Notebooks, and the legacy Prediction service into a single managed environment. Over time, as generative AI exploded, Vertex AI absorbed Generative AI Studio, Model Garden, and the Text-Bison/Chat-Bison family of PaLM models. By 2024–2025, the platform's center of gravity shifted decisively from "train-and-deploy classical ML models" to "build, govern, and operate agentic generative AI systems."

The **Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform** is the natural rebranding and re-architecture of Vertex AI around three realities:

1. **The unit of deployment is an Agent, not a Model.** Enterprises no longer ship "a fine-tuned BERT classifier"; they ship an autonomous reasoning system that plans, calls tools, retrieves context, and orchestrates other agents.
2. **The control plane and data plane are now explicitly separated.** This mirrors how Google runs its own internal AI products (Search, Workspace Gemini, Gemini App) and is critical for VPC-SC, CMEK, and multi-region governance.
3. **Open protocols (MCP, A2A) are first-class.** The platform assumes agents will talk to external tools (via MCP) and to other agents (via A2A), not just call Google-owned APIs.

### 1.2 High-Level Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph CP["Control Plane (Global, Multi-region)"]
        AS[Agent Studio]
        MR[Model Registry]
        RR[RAG Engine / Corpus Mgmt]
        VS[Vector Search Control]
        AR[Agent Revisions]
        EXP[Experiments]
        META[Metadata Store]
        IAM[IAM / CMEK / VPC-SC Policies]
    end

    subgraph DP["Data Plane (Regional, Per-Tenant)"]
        EP[Online Prediction Endpoints]
        RT[Agent Runtime]
        GW[Agent Gateway]
        VSIdx[Vector Search Indexes]
        RAG[RAG Corpora]
        FS[Feature Store]
        SBX[Code Execution Sandbox]
    end

    subgraph EXT["External Integrations"]
        MCP[MCP Servers]
        A2A[A2A Agents]
        GCS[Cloud Storage / Drive / BigQuery]
        THIRD[Third-Party: Anthropic, Meta, Mistral]
    end

    CP <--> DP
    DP <--> EXT
```

### 1.3 Control Plane vs. Data Plane — Why It Matters

The **control plane** is where you *configure* the system: define prompts, register models, create agents, set IAM policies, manage CMEK keys, schedule evaluations, and approve revisions. Operations here are eventually-consistent and global — a prompt version created in `us-central1` is visible in `europe-west4` within seconds.

The **data plane** is where *inference happens*: online prediction calls, vector queries, agent step execution, RAG retrieval, and tool invocations. Data-plane components are **regional** and **per-tenant isolated**. This separation is what allows a regulated European customer to keep all inference traffic inside EU boundaries (via VPC-SC) while still using a single global control plane managed by their US-based platform team.

**Production implication**: When designing for high availability, you must replicate *both* planes. A common mistake is to deploy endpoints in multiple regions but forget that the Vector Search index or RAG corpus lives in a single region — failover then breaks retrieval. The right pattern is to create per-region data-plane resources and use the Agent Gateway to route traffic.

sections.title: 2. Foundation Models
sections.body:
### 2.1 Gemini Model Family Overview

The Gemini family is Google's flagship multimodal model series. As of 2026, the production line-up includes:

| Model | Context Window | Modalities | Primary Use Case | Approx. Pricing (per 1M tok) |
|-------|---------------|------------|------------------|------------------------------|
| Gemini 3.6 Flash | 2M tokens | Text, Image, Audio, Video | General-purpose agentic workloads, high-volume reasoning | Input ~$0.20, Output ~$0.60 |
| Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite | 1M tokens | Text, Image, Audio | Cost-optimized classification, extraction, simple agents | Input ~$0.075, Output ~$0.30 |
| Gemini 2.5 Pro | 2M tokens | Text, Image, Audio, Video | Highest-quality reasoning, complex coding, long-context analysis | Input ~$1.25, Output ~$5.00 |
| Gemini Thinking Models (variants of 2.5/3.x) | 2M tokens | Text, Image, Audio | Multi-step reasoning with visible chain-of-thought | Slight premium over base |

### 2.2 Gemini 3.6 Flash — Internal Architecture

Gemini 3.6 Flash is a **Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Transformer** with the following key architectural properties:

- **Sparse MoE routing**: Only a subset of expert feed-forward layers is activated per token. This decouples parameter count from FLOPs, allowing a model with hundreds of billions of parameters to run at the inference cost of a much smaller dense model.
- **Native multimodal encoders**: Text, image patches, audio spectrograms, and video frames are projected into a shared embedding space before entering the transformer stack. There is no separate "vision encoder" bolted on — this is why Gemini can reason across modalities without re-encoding.
- **Long-context attention**: Uses a combination of Ring Attention, sparse attention patterns, and KV-cache sharding across TPUs to support 2M-token contexts without OOM.
- **Tool-use pretraining**: The model was trained with synthetic tool-calling trajectories, so function calling, code execution, and structured output (JSON schema) are native capabilities rather than prompt-engineered hacks.

#### Request Lifecycle (Gemini 3.6 Flash)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Gateway as Agent Gateway
    participant Auth as IAM/Token Broker
    participant Router as Model Router
    participant Flash as Gemini 3.6 Flash Endpoint
    participant TPU as TPU Pod
    participant Tools as Tool Layer (MCP/Function)

    Client->>Gateway: POST /v1/models/gemini-3.6-flash:generateContent
    Gateway->>Auth: Validate OAuth token + IAM roles
    Auth-->>Gateway: Valid + quota check
    Gateway->>Router: Route by model ID, region, latency SLO
    Router->>Flash: Forward request + telemetry headers
    Flash->>TPU: Prefill (prompt) on TPU pod
    Flash->>Tools: Optional: parallel tool calls during generation
    Tools-->>Flash: Tool results
    Flash->>TPU: Decode tokens (streaming)
    Flash-->>Gateway: Stream chunks (SSE)
    Gateway-->>Client: Streamed response + usage metadata
```

#### Python Example: Streaming Multimodal Call

```python
from google import genai
from google.genai.types import (
    GenerateContentConfig,
    Part,
    Content,
    HttpOptions,
    SafetySetting,
    HarmCategory,
    HarmBlockThreshold,
)
import base64, httpx, asyncio

# Initialize the Google Gen AI SDK (v2 SDK, used by Agent Platform)
client = genai.Client(
    vertexai=True,  # Use Vertex/Agent Platform backend
    project="my-enterprise-project",
    location="us-central1",
    http_options=HttpOptions(api_version="v1"),
)

# Load an image and encode as Part
image_bytes = httpx.get("https://example.com/financial-chart.png").content
image_part = Part.from_bytes(data=image_bytes, mime_type="image/png")

# Build the request
contents = [
    Content(role="user", parts=[
        Part.from_text(text="Analyze this chart. Identify trend reversals and cite exact dates."),
        image_part,
    ])
]

# Strict JSON schema for structured output
response_schema = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
        "reversals": {
            "type": "array",
            "items": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "date": {"type": "string"},
                    "direction": {"type": "string", "enum": ["bullish", "bearish"]},
                    "confidence": {"type": "number"},
                    "rationale": {"type": "string"},
                },
                "required": ["date", "direction", "confidence", "rationale"],
            },
        },
    },
    "required": ["reversals"],
}

# Safety settings — enterprise-grade blocking
safety = [
    SafetySetting(category=HarmCategory.HARM_CATEGORY_HARASSMENT,
                  threshold=HarmBlockThreshold.BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH),
    SafetySetting(category=HarmCategory.HARM_CATEGORY_DANGEROUS_CONTENT,
                  threshold=HarmBlockThreshold.BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE),
]

config = GenerateContentConfig(
    temperature=0.2,
    max_output_tokens=4096,
    top_p=0.95,
    response_mime_type="application/json",
    response_schema=response_schema,
    safety_settings=safety,
    thinking_config={"thinking_budget": 2048},  # explicit thinking tokens
)

# Stream the response
async def stream():
    async for chunk in client.aio.models.generate_content_stream(
        model="gemini-3.6-flash",
        contents=contents,
        config=config,
    ):
        if chunk.text:
            print(chunk.text, end="", flush=True)

asyncio.run(stream())
```

#### Key Operational Notes

- **Thinking Budget**: Gemini 3.6 Flash supports an explicit `thinking_budget` token allotment. Setting it to 0 disables thinking; setting it higher improves reasoning quality at the cost of latency and tokens billed. For deterministic extraction tasks, set it to 0; for multi-step reasoning, use 2048–8192.
- **KV Cache Reuse**: When making repeated calls with the same long prefix (e.g., a 100K-token legal document), enable implicit context caching — the platform caches the KV state for 1 hour by default and bills subsequent calls at a steep discount.
- **Quota Headers**: Every response includes `X-Quota-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`. For production services, build a token-bucket rate limiter in the Agent Gateway that reads these headers and sheds load proactively.

### 2.3 Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite — When to Use It

Flash-Lite is the cost-optimized member of the Flash family. It uses a smaller expert count and a distilled training corpus. Use cases where it shines:

- **Log classification and routing**: Triage incoming support tickets, classify severity, route to queue. Latency-critical, accuracy-tolerant.
- **PII redaction pre-pass**: Run Flash-Lite on raw text to identify and mask PII before passing to a more expensive model for the actual task.
- **Embedding-quality text cleaning**: Strip markdown, normalize whitespace, summarize long documents before embedding.
- **High-volume structured extraction**: Pull fields from semi-structured emails or forms where the schema is well-known and the variability is low.

**Avoid** Flash-Lite for: complex multi-hop reasoning, agentic planning, code generation, or any task where a 1–2% accuracy drop cascades into a much larger downstream cost.

### 2.4 Gemini 2.5 Pro — The Reasoning Workhorse

Gemini 2.5 Pro is the highest-quality model in the family. It is the model to default to when:

- You need **long-context deep reasoning** (e.g., "read this 1.5M-token codebase and identify all SQL injection vulnerabilities with file:line citations").
- You are doing **complex code generation** spanning multiple files, with cross-file type dependencies.
- You are running **multi-step agentic planning** where each reasoning step compounds errors.

#### Thinking Models — What's Different

Gemini Thinking Models expose their chain-of-thought as a separate, addressable field in the response. The thinking trace is **not** mixed into the visible output, which has three important consequences:

1. **Auditability**: You can log the thinking trace for compliance without polluting the user-facing response.
2. **Cost control**: Thinking tokens are billed at a lower rate than output tokens but still cost money. Tune `thinking_budget` per workload.
3. **Safety**: The thinking trace can be independently scanned for prompt-injection attempts or leakage of sensitive context.

```python
response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.5-pro",
    contents="Design a distributed rate limiter that handles 1M req/s with sub-10ms p99 latency. Walk through every design decision.",
    config=GenerateContentConfig(
        thinking_config={"thinking_budget": 8192, "include_thoughts": True},
    ),
)

for part in response.candidates[0].content.parts:
    if part.thought:
        print("=== THINKING ===")
        print(part.thought)
    else:
        print("=== ANSWER ===")
        print(part.text)
```

### 2.5 Imagen — Image Generation

Imagen is Google's diffusion-based text-to-image model. The current production version (Imagen 4) produces photorealistic images with strong text rendering, multi-aspect-ratio support, and style transfer capabilities.

#### Architecture at a Glance

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    P[Prompt] --> PE[Prompt Encoder / T5]
    PE --> CA[Cross-Attention Layers]
    N[Noise Tensor z_T] --> DM[Diffusion U-Net / Transformer]
    CA --> DM
    DM -->|iterative denoising| Z0[Latent z_0]
    Z0 --> VAE[VAE Decoder]
    VAE --> IMG[Output Image]
    IMG --> SAF[Safety Classifier]
    SAF -->|pass| OUT[Final Image]
    SAF -->|block| REJ[Reject + Log]
```

#### Python Example

```python
from google.genai.types import GenerateImagesConfig, Image

response = client.models.generate_images(
    model="imagen-4.0-generate-001",
    prompt="A photorealistic photograph of a modern data center aisle, blue LED lighting, wide-angle, shot on Sony A7R IV, 16-35mm lens",
    config=GenerateImagesConfig(
        number_of_images=4,
        aspect_ratio="16:9",
        safety_filter_level="block_only_high",
        person_generation="allow_adult",
        add_watermark=True,  # required for production deployments
        output_options={"mime_type": "image/png"},
    ),
)

for i, img in enumerate(response.generated_images):
    with open(f"/tmp/imagen_{i}.png", "wb") as f:
        f.write(img.image.image_bytes)
```

**Enterprise considerations**:
- Always enable `add_watermark=True` for public-facing images — SynthID watermarking is invisible but detectable, and is required by several regulatory frameworks.
- `person_generation` defaults to `allow_adult` but can be locked to `dont_allow` at the org policy level. For financial services, this is often a hard compliance requirement.
- Imagen bills per image, not per token. Batch size matters for cost; use `number_of_images=4` to amortize prompt encoding.

### 2.6 Veo — Video Generation

Veo is Google's video generation model (Veo 3 is current). It produces up to 1080p video with synchronized audio from text prompts, supporting camera control, style references, and clip extension.

```python
# Veo is invoked asynchronously — video generation takes minutes
operation = client.models.generate_videos(
    model="veo-3.0-generate-001",
    prompt="A drone shot flying over a snowy mountain range at sunrise, cinematic, 8 seconds",
    config={
        "number_of_videos": 1,
        "duration_seconds": 8,
        "aspect_ratio": "16:9",
        "resolution": "720p",
        "generate_audio": True,
    },
)

# Poll for completion
import time
while not operation.done:
    time.sleep(15)
    operation = client.operations.get(operation)

video = operation.response.generated_videos[0]
print(video.video.uri)  # GCS URI of the generated video
```

**Production pattern**: Veo operations can take 2–5 minutes. Never call it synchronously from a request handler. Instead, enqueue the request, return a job ID, and use Cloud Tasks + a polling worker. Store the result URI in GCS with a TTL and serve via Signed URLs.

### 2.7 Embeddings — gemini-embedding-001 / 002

The Gemini embedding models produce state-of-the-art dense vectors used for retrieval, classification, clustering, and anomaly detection. Key facts:

- **gemini-embedding-001**: 3072-dimensional output, supports task type signals (`RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT`, `RETRIEVAL_QUERY`, `SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY`, `CLASSIFICATION`, `CLUSTERING`, `QUESTION_ANSWERING`, `FACT_VERIFICATION`).
- **gemini-embedding-002**: Improved multilingual coverage and longer input support (up to 8K tokens). Recommended for new deployments.

#### Why Task Type Matters

The same text encoded as a "retrieval document" vs. a "retrieval query" produces **different vectors**. The model is trained asymmetrically: queries are short and information-seeking; documents are long and information-bearing. Using the wrong task type can drop recall by 20–40%.

```python
from google.genai.types import EmbedContentConfig

# Index a corpus of documents
docs = ["Q3 revenue was $4.2B, up 18% YoY", "The new SaaS tier launches in Q4", ...]

doc_embeddings = []
for doc in docs:
    resp = client.models.embed_content(
        model="gemini-embedding-002",
        contents=doc,
        config=EmbedContentConfig(
            task_type="RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT",
            output_dimensionality=768,  # Matryoshka: smaller = faster, slightly less accurate
        ),
    )
    doc_embeddings.append(resp.embeddings[0].values)

# At query time
query_resp = client.models.embed_content(
    model="gemini-embedding-002",
    contents="What was Q3 revenue?",
    config=EmbedContentConfig(
        task_type="RETRIEVAL_QUERY",
        output_dimensionality=768,
    ),
)
```

#### Matryoshka Embeddings

Gemini embeddings support **Matryoshka representation learning** — the first N dimensions of the vector are a valid, lower-dimensional embedding. This lets you trade storage/retrieval speed for accuracy:

| Dimension | Recall@10 (vs 3072) | Storage | Latency |
|-----------|---------------------|---------|---------|
| 3072 (full) | 100% | 12 KB/doc | 1.0x |
| 1536 | ~98% | 6 KB/doc | 0.7x |
| 768 | ~95% | 3 KB/doc | 0.5x |
| 256 | ~88% | 1 KB/doc | 0.3x |

For most enterprise RAG workloads, 768 dimensions is the sweet spot.

sections.title: 3. Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Core
sections.body:
### 3.1 Agent Platform Architecture (Control vs. Data Plane) — Deep Dive The Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform is built on a strict control-plane/data-plane separation. This is not a marketing distinction; it is a fundamental architectural decision that affects every operational concern from billing to security to multi-region failover. #### Control Plane Components 1. **Agent Studio** (formerly Vertex AI Studio): The web UI for interactive prompt design, model testing, agent authoring, and evaluation. Backed by a managed backend that persists all artifacts in customer-owned GCS buckets. 2. **Model Registry**: A versioned catalog of all models available to the project — Google first-party, partner models, and custom-tuned models. Each model has versions, aliases (e.g., `production`, `staging`), and metadata (framework, input/output schema, evaluation metrics). 3. **Agent Revisions**: Every saved configuration of an agent is an immutable revision. Revisions can be tagged, compared, deployed, rolled back. Think git commits for agents. 4. **RAG Corpus Management**: Control-plane API to create, configure, and delete RAG corpora. The actual data (chunks, embeddings) lives in regional data-plane storage. 5. **Vector Search Control Plane**: Index creation, update scheduling, and metadata. Indexes themselves live in regional data-plane deployments. 6. **Experiments & Metadata Store**: Tracks every training run, evaluation, deployment, and A/B test as a first-class artifact with lineage. 7. **IAM, CMEK, VPC-SC Policies**: All governance is enforced at the control plane. The data plane inherits these policies and cannot override them. #### Data Plane Components 1. **Online Prediction Endpoints**: Regional, autoscaling inference servers. Each endpoint hosts one or more model deployments (the model ID + a specific revision + a machine type + autoscaling config). 2. **Agent Runtime**: The execution engine that runs agent loops — receives a user message, calls the LLM, parses tool calls, executes tools, returns the result. Stateless per-request, with state persisted externally (Sessions, Memory Bank). 3. **Agent Gateway**: An HTTPS front-door that handles auth, quota, routing, traffic splitting, and telemetry. This is the single entry point for all production traffic to agents. 4. **Vector Search Indexes**: The actual ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) data structures serving queries. Each index is deployed to a specific region with configurable machine type and replica count. 5. **RAG Corpora**: The managed data stores holding ingested documents, chunked and embedded. Backed by Spanner for metadata and GCS for chunk content. 6. **Code Execution Sandbox**: A hardened, ephemeral container that executes Python code generated by the agent. Network-isolated, resource-limited, logs streamed back. 7. **Feature Store**: Low-latency key/value store for online features (e.g., user profile, recent activity). Used by retrieval-augmented agents to personalize context. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph CP["Control Plane"] direction TB Studio[Agent Studio] Reg[Model Registry] Rev[Agent Revisions] RagCtrl[RAG Corpus Mgmt] VSCtrl[Vector Search Control] Exp[Experiments] Meta[Metadata Store] Pol[IAM/CMEK/VPC-SC] end subgraph DP1["Data Plane — us-central1"] EP1[Endpoints] RT1[Agent Runtime] GW1[Agent Gateway] VSI1[Vector Indexes] RAG1[RAG Corpora] end subgraph DP2["Data Plane — europe-west4"] EP2[Endpoints] RT2[Agent Runtime] GW2[Agent Gateway] VSI2[Vector Indexes] RAG2[RAG Corpora] end CP --> DP1 CP --> DP2 User[End User] --> GW1 User --> GW2 ``` ### 3.2 Agent Studio (formerly Vertex AI Studio) Agent Studio is the primary web-based authoring environment. It is the evolution of what was called "Vertex AI Studio" — the rebrand reflects the shift from "test prompts against models" to "build, debug, and ship agents." #### Capabilities - **Free-form Prompt Playground**: Send multimodal content (text, image, audio, video) to any model in Model Garden. Inspect token probabilities, safety scores, and thinking traces. - **Structured Prompt Design**: Build prompts with explicit input variables, system instructions, and few-shot examples. Save as versioned Prompt Templates. - **Agent Builder**: A visual canvas for composing agents — define tools, sessions, memory, retrieval, and reasoning strategy. Generates deployable agent configurations. - **Tuning**: Initiate supervised fine-tuning or RLHF tuning jobs on Google models with your own data. - **Evaluation Studio**: Run batch evaluations against a curated dataset, compute metrics (faithfulness, groundedness, latency, cost), and compare model revisions side-by-side. - **Multi-modal Inspection**: Upload an image/audio file and see how the model tokenizes and reasons about it — useful for debugging vision/audio pipelines. #### Request Lifecycle in Agent Studio When you click "Run" in Agent Studio: 1. The browser POSTs to the Studio backend (control plane). 2. The backend validates your IAM permissions for the target model. 3. The request is forwarded to the appropriate regional data-plane endpoint. 4. The response is streamed back to the browser via Server-Sent Events. 5. The full request/response is logged to your project's GCS bucket (`gs://cloud-ai-platform-staging-...`) for later inspection or for use as a few-shot example. ### 3.3 Prompt Engineering on Agent Platform Effective prompt engineering on the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform goes far beyond "write a good prompt." The platform provides structured primitives that make prompts versioned, parameterized, evaluated, and governable. #### Prompt Anatomy ```mermaid flowchart TB SI[System Instructions
persistent context
role, rules, tone] CTX[Context Variables
injected at runtime
user profile, retrieved docs] FS[Few-Shot Examples
input/output pairs
curated for the task] USR[User Input
the actual query] OUT[Output Config
JSON schema, temperature,
max tokens, safety] P[Final Prompt] = SI + CTX + FS + USR + OUT ``` #### Best Practices Specific to Gemini 3.x 1. **System instructions over prefix instructions**: Gemini 3.x has a dedicated `system_instruction` field that is treated with higher priority than user-content during instruction hierarchy resolution. Always put core rules there. 2. **Explicit role tags**: Use `role: "user"`, `role: "model"`, and (for agents) `role: "function"` consistently. The model is trained on this format and degrades when you mix conventions. 3. **Schema-driven output**: When you need structured output, pass `response_schema` and `response_mime_type="application/json"`. The model is constraint-decoded to produce valid JSON; you eliminate an entire class of parsing failures. 4. **Thinking budget for reasoning tasks**: For multi-step reasoning, set `thinking_budget >= 4096`. The model uses these tokens invisibly before emitting output. 5. **Few-shot > zero-shot for edge cases**: For tasks with subtle formatting or domain conventions, 2–4 high-quality few-shot examples outperform elaborate instructions. ### 3.4 Prompt Gallery The Prompt Gallery is a managed repository of curated, reusable prompt templates contributed by Google and by your organization. Each entry includes: - The prompt template (with placeholders) - Recommended model and parameters - Example inputs and outputs - Evaluation scores on a standard benchmark - Tags for discoverability (e.g., `summarization`, `code-generation`, `multilingual`) **Enterprise pattern**: Establish an internal "Prompt Guild" that reviews and approves prompts before they enter the org-level Prompt Gallery. This creates a curated catalog that new teams can build on, rather than every team reinventing the summarization prompt from scratch. ### 3.5 Prompt Templates A Prompt Template is a parameterized, versioned prompt definition stored in the control plane. It decouples the prompt (owned by prompt engineers/PMs) from the application code (owned by developers). #### Structure ```python template = { "name": "projects/my-project/locations/us-central1/prompts/summarize-filing", "version": "v3", "system_instruction": "You are a financial analyst. Summarize SEC filings concisely.", "placeholders": [ {"name": "filing_text", "type": "STRING", "required": True}, {"name": "max_sentences", "type": "INTEGER", "default": 5}, ], "prompt_text": "Summarize the following filing in at most {{max_sentences}} sentences:\n\n{{filing_text}}", "model": "gemini-3.6-flash", "generation_config": {"temperature": 0.1, "max_output_tokens": 1024}, } ``` #### Using a Template from Code ```python from google.cloud import aiplatform_v1 # Load the prompt version prompt_client = aiplatform_v1.PromptServiceClient(client_options={ "api_endpoint": "us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com" }) prompt_version = prompt_client.get_prompt_version( name="projects/my-project/locations/us-central1/prompts/summarize-filing@v3" ) # Render and call filled = prompt_version.prompt_text.replace("{{filing_text}}", filing_text).replace("{{max_sentences}}", "5") response = client.models.generate_content( model=prompt_version.model, contents=filled, config=GenerateContentConfig(**prompt_version.generation_config), ) ``` ### 3.6 Prompt Versioning Every save to a Prompt Template creates a new immutable version. Versions are addressable as `prompts/{name}@{version}`. The platform supports: - **Aliases**: Tag a version as `production`, `staging`, `experiment-2026-q1`. Code references the alias; ops teams re-point aliases to roll forward or back. - **Diffing**: Visual diff between any two versions in Agent Studio. - **Lineage**: Each version records who created it, from what base, with what evaluation scores. This is critical for compliance audits. - **Approval workflows**: Optional — require a second reviewer's approval before a version can be aliased to `production`. ### 3.7 Prompt Evaluation The platform's evaluation framework lets you score prompt versions against curated test sets before deploying. Built-in metrics include: - **Exact Match / ROUGE / BLEU** for traditional NLG tasks - **LLM-as-judge** metrics (faithfulness, groundedness, helpfulness) using a strong judge model (typically Gemini 2.5 Pro) - **Custom metrics** defined as Python callables or as additional LLM-judge prompts - **Trajectory metrics** for agent prompts (tool-call correctness, step count, cost) ```python from google.cloud import aiplatform_v1 eval_client = aiplatform_v1.EvalServiceClient(client_options={ "api_endpoint": "us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com" }) eval_run = eval_client.create_evaluation( parent="projects/my-project/locations/us-central1", evaluation={ "display_name": "summarize-filing-v3-vs-v4", "prompt_versions": [ "projects/.../prompts/summarize-filing@v3", "projects/.../prompts/summarize-filing@v4", ], "dataset": {"gcs_source": {"uris": ["gs://my-bucket/eval/summaries.jsonl"]}}, "metrics": ["faithfulness", "groundedness", "rouge_l", "latency_p95"], "judge_model": "gemini-2.5-pro", }, ) ``` The result is a side-by-side report showing which version wins on each metric, with statistical significance. Promote the winner to `production` only after this gate.

sections.title: 4. Model Garden
sections.body:
### 4.1 Overview

Model Garden is the platform's catalog of all available models — first-party Google models, open models (Gemma, Llama), and partner models (Claude from Anthropic, Mistral, Jamba from AI21, etc.). Every model in Model Garden is callable via a uniform API surface, which is the key value proposition: your application code stays the same whether you switch from Gemini to Claude to Llama.

### 4.2 Google First-Party Models

This category includes the entire Gemini family, Gemma (open weights), and specialized models like ShieldGemma (safety classification), PaliGemma (vision-language), and the Embedding models.

#### Gemma — Open-Weight Models

Gemma is Google's open-weight model family. As of 2026, Gemma 3 is current, with sizes from 1B to 27B parameters. Gemma models are downloadable and can be:

- **Self-hosted** on GKE, GCE with GPUs, or on-prem.
- **Fine-tuned** via supervised tuning or LoRA.
- **Deployed to Agent Platform endpoints** for managed serving (the platform handles infra, you bring the weights).

```python
# Deploy a fine-tuned Gemma to a Vertex endpoint
from google.cloud import aiplatform

model = aiplatform.Model.upload(
    display_name="gemma-3-27b-finetuned-legal",
    serving_container_image_uri="us-docker.pkg.dev/vertex-ai/prediction/vllm-cpu.0-6.ubuntu2204",
    artifact_uri="gs://my-bucket/gemma-legal-weights/",
    serving_container_environment_variables={
        "MODEL_ID": "gemma-legal",
        "PORT": "8080",
    },
)

endpoint = aiplatform.Endpoint.create(display_name="gemma-legal-endpoint")
model.deploy(
    endpoint=endpoint,
    machine_type="a3-highgpu-2g",
    accelerator_type="NVIDIA_H100_80GB",
    accelerator_count=2,
    min_replica_count=1,
    max_replica_count=4,
)
```

### 4.3 Partner Models

The Agent Platform hosts partner models as **managed API gateways** — the request flows through Google's auth, quota, and billing infrastructure, but inference happens on the partner's infrastructure (e.g., Anthropic's Claude runs on AWS Bedrock behind the scenes, transparently).

| Partner | Models | Why Choose |
|---------|--------|------------|
| Anthropic | Claude Opus, Sonnet, Haiku | Strong reasoning, long-context coding, Constitutional AI safety |
| Meta | Llama 3.1/3.2/3.3 | Open weights, self-hostable, large ecosystem |
| Mistral | Mistral Large, Codestral, Mixtral | European data residency, strong code generation |
| AI21 | Jamba | SSM+Transformer hybrid, very long context |
| Cohere | Command R+ | Strong retrieval-tuned performance |
| ElevenLabs | TTS models | Best-in-class voice generation |

#### Calling a Partner Model (Claude Example)

```python
# Same SDK, different model name — that's the whole point of Model Garden
response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="claude-3-5-sonnet-v2@20241022",  # Anthropic model, Google API
    contents="Explain quantum entanglement to a 12-year-old.",
    config=GenerateContentConfig(temperature=0.7, max_output_tokens=1024),
)
```

#### Architecture — How Partner Calls Work

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant App
    participant GW as Agent Gateway
    participant Quota as Quota Service
    participant Router as Model Router
    participant Anth as Anthropic Backend (via Bedrock)
    participant BQ as BigQuery (Audit Log)

    App->>GW: POST /v1/models/claude-3-5-sonnet:generateContent
    GW->>Quota: Check Anthropic quota (separate from Gemini quota)
    Quota-->>GW: OK
    GW->>Router: Route to "anthropic-claude-provider"
    Router->>Anth: Translated Anthropic API call (with Google's credentials)
    Anth-->>Router: Claude response
    Router-->>GW: Normalized to Google GenAI response format
    GW->>BQ: Audit log entry (model, tokens, latency, cost)
    GW-->>App: Response
```

### 4.4 Choosing Between Models — A Decision Framework

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start[Task: Choose Model] --> Q1{Reasoning Complexity?}
    Q1 -->|High: multi-step planning, code gen| Pro[Gemini 2.5 Pro or Claude Opus]
    Q1 -->|Medium: standard tasks| Q2{Cost Sensitive?}
    Q1 -->|Low: extraction, classification| Lite[Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite]

    Q2 -->|Yes| Flash[Gemini 3.6 Flash]
    Q2 -->|No| Q3{Need Long Context >1M tokens?}
    Q3 -->|Yes| Flash
    Q3 -->|No| Q4{European data residency required?}
    Q4 -->|Yes| Mistral[Mistral Large]
    Q4 -->|No| Sonnet[Claude Sonnet]

    Pro --> Final[Run Evaluation]
    Flash --> Final
    Lite --> Final
    Sonnet --> Final
    Mistral --> Final
```
